card.occupation: Chartered accountant (audit senior manager) at a mid-sized accountancy firm near Liverpool Street
card.education_detail: BSc Accounting and Finance from a university in Lahore, then an MSc in Accounting from a London university after moving to the UK at 22; qualified as an ACA chartered accountant through his firm's training scheme
card.household: Lives with his wife Hira, 28, a hospital pharmacist, in a two-bedroom rented flat off Cranbrook Road. They have been married three years and have no children yet. His older brother and his family live ten minutes away in Gants Hill.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in Lahore, Pakistan, in a middle-class Punjabi family; his father ran a small textiles business. Came to London for his master's and stayed for work. A practising Sunni Muslim who prays regularly, goes to the local mosque for Jummah when his schedule allows, and fasts during Ramadan. Speaks Punjabi and Urdu at home with family, mostly English with Hira day to day. Now a British citizen, but still thinks of Lahore as home in some ways.
card.professional_persona: Steady, careful auditor who has worked at the same firm since qualifying. Mainly works on manufacturing and logistics clients. Known for being straight with clients and for not cutting corners. Juniors find him approachable. He doesn't chase the spotlight and is a bit uncomfortable with the networking side of the job. Hybrid working: three days in the office, two from home.
card.sports_persona: Lifelong cricket fan. Follows Pakistan closely and stays up for matches in other time zones. Plays in a Sunday-league tape-ball and softball cricket group in Valentines Park through the summer. Not into football beyond knowing the Premier League table from office chat. Goes on a brisk walk most evenings.
card.arts_persona: Not much of an arts person. Watches the same few things: cricket highlights, the odd Pakistani drama that Hira puts on, and action films at the Ilford cinema. Listens to nasheeds and Quran recitation on the commute, plus old Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan because his dad played it. Hasn't been to a gallery since a uni trip and doesn't feel he's missing anything.
card.travel_persona: Travel mostly means going back to Lahore once a year, usually for a wedding or Eid, to see his parents. He and Hira did Umrah together two years ago, which he counts as the most important trip of his life. One holiday to Istanbul because friends recommended it. Prefers places where he knows the food is halal and he knows what to expect.
card.culinary_persona: Likes the food he grew up with: his mum's karahi, daal chawal, and parathas at the weekend. He can cook a decent chicken karahi and makes it most Fridays. Eats on Ilford Lane or in Green Street with his brother. At work he sticks to the same meal deal or a chicken wrap from the same place. Not adventurous. He'll try something new if Hira insists, but usually orders what he had last time.
hobbies_and_interests: helping out at the mosque on Ramadan iftar rotas
keeping the household budget in a spreadsheet
FIFA on the PlayStation with his nephew
skills: Cooking a few Pakistani home dishes well
card.career_goals: Wants to make director at his current firm within five or six years rather than jump around. Mainly cares about stability, a good salary to buy a house in Redbridge, and being able to support his parents. Not interested in starting his own thing.
card.voice: Polite, measured and fairly quiet, with a Lahori accent softened by eight years in London. Speaks at an even pace, a bit slower when he's thinking. Uses 'er' when he hesitates and says 'sort of' and 'you know' now and then. Says 'dinner' for the evening meal and 'mate' with colleagues. Doesn't use slang much. Answers questions directly and then stops. He's comfortable with a short silence and will wait rather than fill it. Sometimes says 'sorry, can you say that again?' if the line is unclear.
card.typing: Mostly proper sentences with a capital at the start, full stops sometimes dropped at the end. Uses apostrophes correctly out of habit from work. Short answers, no emojis. Occasionally 'n/a' or 'approx'. Might write 'Yes, about 2 years' rather than anything longer.
card.with_strangers: Courteous and a little reserved at first. Shakes hands, remembers your name, asks one polite question back. Comes across as sincere and modest. He won't oversell himself and may undersell his job. Warms up once cricket, food or family comes up, but doesn't overshare.
small_things: The Central line being rammed in the mornings
His Sunday cricket game got rained off again
Hira's shift pattern at the hospital
Picking up meat from the halal butcher on Ilford Lane
Busy season at work from January to March
His nephew beating him at FIFA
Staying up till 3am for a Pakistan match
deeper_things: He feels guilty being so far from his ageing parents and worries about his father's diabetes
He and Hira have been hoping for children and it hasn't happened yet
He sometimes feels he doesn't fully belong in Lahore or London anymore
Saving for a house deposit while sending money home is a strain he doesn't talk about
His faith is what keeps him steady when work gets stressful
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at eye level, slightly off-centre, lit by daylight from a window to his left with an overhead ceiling light on. Head and shoulders in frame. A man with light brown skin, short neatly trimmed black hair, and a short tidy beard. Brown eyes, no glasses, a small polite closed-mouth smile. Wearing a plain navy quarter-zip jumper over a white collared shirt. Behind him is a magnolia wall with a framed Arabic calligraphy print in gold on black, a white IKEA bookshelf holding accountancy study manuals, a few box files and a small cricket trophy, and a folded prayer mat on the lower shelf. The corner of a grey radiator is visible at bottom right.
